title: A verifier's refutation text is written unmasked to counts.md, ledger.json and ledger.md, so the claim that everything Curmudgeon writes is masked is false
evidence: apply() masks final, unverified and the refutations.jsonl line, but the refuted list keeps the raw why from the verdict file. Line 339 writes it into counts.md under 'Refuted by verification'. Line 367 passes "refuted by verification: " + r["why"][:200] to critic_ledger.py status, which stores it in ledger.json and renders it into ledger.md. None of these three is in IGNORED. README says everything Curmudgeon writes itself has secrets masked. N-4 covers only a confirmed verdict.
failing_case: Executed in a scratch git repo: app.py:2 holds a fake sk_live_ key; run 1 confirmed; run 2 refuted with a refutation quoting the key; the raw key then appears in .critic/counts.md, .critic/ledger.json and .critic/ledger.md.
remediation: Mask why once when read in apply() (why = redact_finding_text(...)); add a refuted-verdict case to the N-4 test.

title: Finding masking runs the log-line rules over code and prose, so ordinary auth, session and token findings come out garbled, line refs included, and their acted-on tracking is switched off
evidence: redact_finding_text ends with redact_secrets(), written for command lines. Its NAME=value rule treats any name containing token, auth, session, password, secret or key as a credential, with a value pattern that accepts '== req.headers...', 'request.form.get(' and '.js:2'. scrub() applies it to quote, title, evidence, failing_case and remediation, sets quote_redacted, and critic_ledger.quote_present then returns None for any quote containing '[redacted]', so acted skips the finding for good.
failing_case: Executed: auth.js:2 `if (session.token == req.headers.authorization) { return true; }` (no secret). After tally and apply the quote reads `if (session.token =[redacted] req.headers.authorization)...` with quote_redacted true, and evidence 'auth.js:[redacted] ...'. Run 2 deletes the code; acted checks 0 findings. Also `password = request.form.get("password")` and `const sessionId = crypto.randomUUID();` get masked.
remediation: Mask finding text with scan_secrets' provider shapes plus its entropy-gated generic rule only; keep the command-line rules for the run log; mark quote_redacted only when a real secret span was replaced; tell the verifier that a redacted quote means read the file at the line.

quote: if started:  # a review file older than this run is left over from an earlier one: counting it would invent votes
title: Old reviews still count as votes in round 2 and in /curmudgeon:iterate: only start moves reviews aside and sets started_at, and round does neither
evidence: started_at is set and .critic/reviews/ emptied only in critic_ledger.py start (lines 157-163). round (critic_ledger.py:355) does neither. SKILL.md step 8 and iterate run round 2 with fresh reviewers; round 1's review-B and review-C are newer than started_at, so the mtime check accepts them.
failing_case: Executed: start full; A, B, C hold the same finding; tally; critic_ledger.py round; the one fresh reviewer writes review-A.json []; tallying the glob keeps the finding with 2 of 3 votes from round 1.
remediation: Make round move .critic/reviews/* aside (history/run-N/round-M/) and reset started_at; add a round-2 case to the N-1 test.

quote: is the share of 11 checks on how the written teardown follows its required format
title: The README says the report format score is out of 11 checks, but the notes-app row is a review-and-fix run, which eval/score.py scores on 14
evidence: eval/score.py contract() defines 11 checks and adds 'refactoring manifest', 'state ledger' and 'closure table' with --refactored, making 14. The notes app row is labelled review and fix.
failing_case: Reproducing the notes-app score with score.py --suite 1 --refactored gives a fraction out of 14, not 11.
remediation: Say 11 checks (14 for a review-and-fix run, which adds the refactoring manifest, state ledger and closure table).
